41/G.goal: Explain how the Majuli VR tour's system design was framed from objectives and user-informed content scope and then realized through its opening experience, media treatment, navigation and information interfaces, and cybersickness-reducing techniques.
41/G.achieves: It lets the learner connect XR requirements, human factors, and case-study decisions to concrete design choices needed before implementation and optimization.

41/O1.goal: Describe how the Majuli VR tour's design scope was shaped by project objectives, an iterative user-informed process, user categories, and its set of information points.
41/O1.achieves: Lets the learner trace XR system design decisions back to requirements and user research, preparing them to evaluate or propose design choices in the case study.

41/O2.goal: Describe how the tour's opening sequence and preprocessed images, videos, and ambient sounds establish the initial immersive context.
41/O2.achieves: Prepares the learner to design entry experiences and media choices that support quality of experience and realism in an XR system.

41/O3.goal: Describe how the tour's tablet interface, minimaps, arrows, notifications, vehicle-based travel, and location-relevant media support orientation, wayfinding, and content exploration.
41/O3.achieves: Gives the learner a concrete model for designing wayfinding and information-access interfaces that help users build mental models and locate content in an XR environment.

41/O4.goal: Explain how controlled navigation, careful vehicle speed, and consistent visual cues were used to minimize cybersickness in the tour.
41/O4.achieves: Supports the learner's ability to apply human-factor and comfort constraints when designing XR locomotion and interaction.
